output.brief:
The rise in VA-220 failures traces to Pellacott's 2026 valves, not to the new installers or firmware 4.2. Brenmoor's own lab found that about 11% of never-installed Pellacott 2026 valves leak at the seat. Pellacott 2025 valves leaked at 1 in 100, and Durrant-Hale valves at 0 in 100. Claim rates for Pellacott valves are the same across installer and firmware groups. The independent calibration visit found Pellacott's leak-test rig out of service since January 2026 and no VA-220 test program on any other rig. The 2026 certificates repeat four fixed sequences of values, some dating from before the rig failed. The certificates therefore do not reflect real tests. Because the SupplierPath score rewards complete certificates, it rose and unlocked dock-to-stock status.

I am fairly confident (about 85–90%) in this. Unknown: whether the Corlin seal or the Line 3 move causes the leaks, and whether other suppliers' records are also unreliable.

Next steps:
- Keep the six lots on hold, and quarantine all 2026 Pellacott stock.
- Suspend dock-to-stock status for Pellacott.
- Release stock only after Brenmoor's own helium testing.
- Drop the installer remediation plan.
- Require rig logs or witnessed tests in the scoring.
- Spot-check other suppliers.
- Ask Pellacott for a root-cause analysis of the seal and line changes.
